narrative.overview: Specter Black Label is a cinematic, restrained identity for a South African digital growth partner serving law firms. It combines severe carbon surfaces, warm bone typography, Bodoni editorial scale, and rare wine accents to communicate discretion, strategic authority, and modern legal credibility.
keyCharacteristics: Carbon-first surfaces with warm bone text rather than stark white
Oversized Bodoni statements paired with precise Instrument Sans utility copy
Wine used as a rare signal for interaction, emphasis, and conversion
Editorial rules, legal numbering, and generous negative space
Subtle cinematic motion that preserves clarity and reduced-motion support
rules: Use #090a0b as the canonical dark surface and #efece5 as the canonical light text.
Reserve wine for high-value emphasis; it must never become a decorative wash.
Display headlines use Bodoni Moda at regular weight with tight tracking.
Navigation is 13px uppercase and section labels are 12px uppercase with generous tracking.
Primary controls maintain a minimum 44px touch target; conversion buttons use 48px or more.
Keep borders square or nearly square. Avoid card-heavy layouts and soft product-dashboard styling.
Every animation must communicate hierarchy, progression, or feedback and respect prefers-reduced-motion.
Use South African language and context deliberately; do not rely on generic global-agency claims.
dos: Let a single large statement establish each section.
Use editorial lines and numbered sequences to create rhythm.
Keep proof, outcomes, and calls to action specific and credible.
Use the Johannesburg visual as atmosphere, never as a substitute for content.
Keep focus states visible and disclosure controls keyboard operable.
donts: Do not introduce gold, neon, gradients, glass cards, or rounded SaaS chrome.
Do not overuse wine or apply it to long passages of text.
Do not mix in the typography or palette of the rejected concepts.
Do not animate every element or use bouncy, playful easing.
Do not publish invented client logos, awards, statistics, or testimonials.
